title.zh: 同一条街上的两根水管
title.en: Two Water Pipes on the Same Street

dek.zh: 1854年，伦敦南部两家自来水公司的管道铺在同一批街道上，隔壁两户人家喝的水可能完全不同。约翰·斯诺决定用这场没人设计的实验，检验自己倡导了五年的学说。
dek.en: In 1854 the mains of two south London water companies ran down the same streets, so that next-door neighbours might be drinking entirely different water. John Snow set out to use this experiment nobody had designed to test the doctrine he had been arguing for five years.

heading.zh: 一场没人设计、却有人记录的实验
heading.en: An experiment nobody designed, and somebody recorded

paras.zh: 1854年7月，霍乱又回到了伦敦。约翰·斯诺倡导一种关涉供水与霍乱的学说已经五年，这一次他写下的决心很直白：不惜一切力气，弄清供水对疫情进程的确切影响；地点选在“一切条件都如此恰好适合这项调查”的街区；而且要亲自去查，因为他要的是“最令人满意的证明”，来检验这个学说究竟是对还是错。
paras.en: In July 1854 cholera came back to London. John Snow had been advocating a doctrine bearing on how water supply affected cholera for five years, and this time he wrote down his resolve without ornament. He would "spare no exertion which might be necessary to ascertain the exact effect of the water supply on the progress of the epidemic", in places where "all the circumstances were so happily adapted for the inquiry". And he would do the work himself, because he wanted "the most satisfactory proof of the truth or fallacy of the doctrine which I had been advocating for five years."

paras.zh: 他看中的是伦敦南部的一片街区。那里有两家自来水公司，水管各自铺进所有街道，几乎深入每一条巷子和院落；哪栋房子接哪一家，是当年两家公司激烈竞争时由房主或住户定下的。结果，很多房子的水和左右两边的邻居都不一样。斯诺看到的，是一场没有人安排、却已经摆在眼前的对照。难处在于：要把它用起来，就得逐户查清每一栋发生霍乱死亡的房子用的是哪家的水，而很多住户自己也说不清。
paras.en: What he had in view was a stretch of south London served by two water companies. "The pipes of each Company go down all the streets, and into nearly all the courts and alleys." Which company a house took had been settled by the owner or occupier back "when the Water Companies were in active competition", and, as Snow put it, "In many cases a single house has a supply different from that on either side." Nobody had arranged a comparison, yet one was already laid out in front of him. The difficulty was that using it meant learning, house by house, which company supplied each house where a cholera death occurred, and many residents could not say themselves.

paras.zh: 先看水从哪里来。1832年到1849年间，伦敦的供水变动很多：南华克公司与南伦敦公司合并，成立南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司；伦敦桥的水厂被撤除，合并后的公司改从沃克斯霍尔桥上游约半英里、巴特西原野一带的泰晤士河取水；兰贝斯公司则一直在亨格福德市场对面取水。
paras.en: Start with where the water came from. Between 1832 and 1849 London's supply changed a good deal. The Southwark Water Company merged with the South London Water Company to form the Southwark and Vauxhall Company; the works at London Bridge were abolished, and the new company drew from the Thames at Battersea Fields, about half a mile above Vauxhall Bridge. The Lambeth Company went on taking its water opposite Hungerford Market.

paras.zh: 从1849年下半年到1853年8月，伦敦没有霍乱。就在这段间隙里，兰贝斯公司把水厂从亨格福德市场对面迁到泰晤士迪顿，于是得到一份“完全不含伦敦污水”的水。迁址的年份，斯诺在一条脚注里专门纠正过巴利医生：巴利以为兰贝斯公司1849年就已在泰晤士迪顿取水，其实到1852年才迁过去。在两家混供的地区，南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司的管道依旧和兰贝斯的管道一起铺在每一条街上。
paras.en: London was free of cholera from the latter part of 1849 to August 1853. In that interval the Lambeth Company moved its works from opposite Hungerford Market to Thames Ditton, "thus obtaining a supply of water quite free from the sewage of London." Snow was careful about the date. In a footnote he corrected Dr Baly, who had supposed that the Lambeth Company was already drawing from Thames Ditton in 1849; the move, Snow pointed out, did not happen until 1852. Where the two supplies were mixed, the Southwark and Vauxhall pipes still ran down every street alongside Lambeth's.

paras.zh: 在斯诺看来，这个格局再理想不过。两家公司都给富人也给穷人供水，大房子小房子都有；他断言，接这家水和接那家水的人，在房屋、人口和周围的一切物质条件上都没有任何差别，因此想不出比这更能彻底检验供水作用的实验——它是环境“现成摆在观察者面前”的。规模也大得惊人：不少于三十万人，不分男女老幼、职业身份，从体面人家到赤贫者，在没有选择、多数也不知情的情况下分成了两组：一组的水里有伦敦的污水，以及可能来自霍乱病人的任何东西；另一组的水没有这类污物。
paras.en: To Snow the arrangement could hardly have been better. "Each Company supplies both rich and poor, both large houses and small", he wrote, and since there was "no difference whatever" in the houses, the people or their physical surroundings, no experiment could have been devised that would more thoroughly test the effect of water supply on cholera "than this, which circumstances placed ready made before the observer." It was enormous, too: "No fewer than three hundred thousand people of both Sexes, of every age and occupation, and of every rank and station, from gentlefolks down to the very poor, were divided into two groups without their choice, and, in most cases, without their knowledge" — one group drinking water that carried the sewage of London and whatever might have come from cholera patients, the other water free of it.

paras.zh: 他并不是一开始就看清了这一点。斯诺承认，前一年年底白天短，他抽不出时间去查；而且那时他也没有充分意识到两家公司的供水混得这么密，因而没意识到这项调查有多重要。要把这场“大实验”用起来，需要的其实只有一件事：查清每一栋发生霍乱死亡的房子，用的是哪家的水。
paras.en: He had not seen all this at once. Snow admitted that in the short days at the end of the previous year he "could not spare the time to make the inquiry", and that he had not then been fully aware of how intimately the two supplies were mixed, nor therefore how much the inquiry mattered. To turn the experiment to account, one thing alone was needed: "to learn the supply of water to each individual house where a fatal attack of cholera might occur."

paras.zh: 1854年，他从一份名单入手。他向登记总署申请，拿到了两家公司混供地区霍乱死者的住址：一部分刊登在每周公报上，另一些获准抄录。8月中旬，他先查兰贝斯的两个分区——肯宁顿第一区和第二区。到8月12日，这两个分区共死亡44人；他查出其中38户由南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水，4户由兰贝斯公司供水，另有2户用自家院里的水井，不接任何一家公司的水。
paras.en: In 1854 he started from a list. He asked the General Register Office for the addresses of people who had died of cholera in the districts where the two supplies were intermingled; some had been printed in the Weekly Returns, and he was allowed to copy others. About the middle of August he began with two sub-districts of Lambeth, Kennington first part and Kennington second part. There had been 44 deaths there down to 12 August. Of the houses where they occurred, he found 38 supplied by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company, 4 by the Lambeth Company, and 2 with pump-wells on the premises and no company supply at all.

paras.zh: 他一弄清这些数字，就告诉了法尔医生（Dr. Farr）。斯诺记下法尔对结果“深受触动”，并在法尔的建议下，伦敦南部各区的登记员被要求在每一例霍乱死亡中登记发病所在房屋的供水。这项规定定于8月26日以后才实行，所以斯诺决定把自己的调查一直做到这一天，好让整场疫情的事实都有据可查。
paras.en: As soon as he had these particulars he passed them to Dr Farr, who, Snow wrote, "was much struck with the result". At Farr's suggestion the registrars of all the south districts of London were asked to return the water supply of the house in which the attack took place, in every death from cholera. The order was to take effect only after 26 August, so Snow resolved to carry his own inquiry down to that date, "so that the facts might be ascertained for the whole course of the epidemic."

paras.zh: 他把调查扩展到兰贝斯、南华克和纽因顿其他混供的分区，结果与肯宁顿“非常相似”。有些病人发病后被送进济贫院或别处，他就去查发病时所住那栋房子的水，而不是他们后来被送去的地方。
paras.en: He carried the inquiry over the other intermixed sub-districts of Lambeth, Southwark and Newington, "with a result very similar to that already given". Where a patient had been moved to a workhouse or anywhere else after the attack began, he asked about the water of the house where the person had been living when it started, not the place they had been moved to.

paras.zh: 麻烦出在归类。很少有人家能当场答出自家用哪家公司的水；就算水费是住户自己交，他们通常也得翻出收据才想得起公司名字。按周交房租的工人家庭更难：水费一律由房东或其代理人缴纳，房东往往住得很远，住户对此一无所知。斯诺写道，要不是发现能用化学检验把两家的水确定无疑地分开，这项调查几乎不可能完成。
paras.en: The hard part was classification. Very few households could name their water company on the spot: "Even when the water-rates are paid by the residents, they can seldom remember the name of the Water Company till they have looked for the receipt." For working families who paid weekly rents it was worse. The rates were paid by the landlord or his agent, who often lived at a distance, "and the residents know nothing about the matter." Snow wrote that it would have been almost impossible to finish the inquiry had he not found that a chemical test could tell the two waters apart with certainty.

paras.zh: 检验靠的是两种水里氯化钠——也就是食盐——含量的巨大差别。往水里加硝酸银，两家的水反应差得很远，一眼就能分辨。住户说不清时，他就用小瓶装一点水，在瓶盖上写下地址，回家再验。他也看水的样子，尤其是刚流进来、还没进水桶或水箱的时候；他还摸清了两家公司的放水工各在几点到哪条街，水来的时辰也能透露是哪家的水。不过这些只用来佐证更确凿的证据，不单独作数。
paras.en: "The test I employed was founded on the great difference in the quantity of chloride of sodium contained in the two kinds of water" — common salt. Add nitrate of silver and the two waters looked so different that they "could be at once distinguished without any further trouble." When a resident could not say for certain, Snow put some water in a small phial, wrote the address on the cover and examined it at home. He looked at the water itself, especially as it came in, before it reached the butt or cistern; and once he had learned the hours when each company's turncocks visited a street, the time the water arrived told him something too. These signs he used only to corroborate more decisive proof, never on their own.

paras.zh: 疫情头七周的结果，他整理成一张表。南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水40,046户，霍乱死亡1,263人；兰贝斯公司供水26,107户，死亡98人。折算成每10,000户的死亡数，分别是315和37；伦敦其余地区为每万户59。OCR文本中“伦敦其余地区”一行的户数与死亡数无法复算出59，可能有识别错误，所以本篇只引用该行的每万户数。不过，南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司的头七周数字并非全部逐户查得。在部分只由该公司供水的分区，怀廷医生的调查只做到8月5日，后三周的供水是按头四周的比例推算的；斯诺认为这一推算“必定非常接近真实”。他据此得出结论：南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水户的死亡率是兰贝斯公司供水户的八到九倍。但这只是疫情头七周的结果。斯诺自己说明，随着疫情推进，两组的悬殊“没那么大了”，不过仍然十分显著。疫情头四周是每万户71对5，相差十四倍；第二个七周是每万户537对115，接近五倍。截至10月14日的14周里，按每万居民计，南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水户死亡153人，兰贝斯公司供水户死亡26人。这组数字把795例供水不明的死亡平均分摊到其他各供水来源，两家公司供水户的人口也是登记总长的估计数。兰贝斯供水户的死亡率低于全伦敦，但并不低于北区和中区。
paras.en: The first seven weeks of the epidemic went into a single table. Houses supplied by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company: 40,046, with 1,263 deaths from cholera. Lambeth Company: 26,107 houses, 98 deaths. Per 10,000 houses that came to 315 and 37; the rest of London stood at 59 per 10,000 houses. In the OCR text the house count and death count in the rest-of-London row cannot be recalculated to give 59 and may have been misread, so only that row's figure per 10,000 houses is cited here. Not all of the Southwark and Vauxhall figures for the first seven weeks were checked house by house, though. In some sub-districts supplied only by that company, the inquiry of a medical man, Mr Whiting, extended only to 5 August, and the water supply of the last three weeks was calculated in the same proportion as in the first four weeks; Snow judged that this calculation "must be very near the truth". Snow's conclusion: "The mortality in the houses supplied by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company was therefore between eight and nine times as great as in the houses supplied by the Lambeth Company". That was the figure for the first seven weeks only. Snow himself wrote that as the epidemic advanced the disproportion "became not quite so great, although it continued very striking". In the first four weeks it had been 71 against 5 per 10,000 houses, fourteen times. In the second seven weeks it was 537 against 115 per 10,000 houses, nearly five times. Over the 14 weeks ending 14 October, there were 153 deaths per 10,000 living in houses supplied by Southwark and Vauxhall and 26 in houses supplied by Lambeth. These figures distribute the 795 deaths whose water supply was not ascertained equally over the other sources of supply, and the population of the houses supplied by the two companies is the Registrar General's estimate. The Lambeth figure was lower than London at large, but not lower than the north and central districts.

paras.zh: 作者的解读：两组数字方向一致。肯宁顿的38户对4户，来自同一片混供街区；不过肯宁顿的数字只是死亡户数，证据未给出两家在当地各有多少供水户，不能直接当作死亡率比较。表里的315对37，覆盖两家公司的供水户，而伦敦其余地区的59恰好落在两者之间。接兰贝斯水的人家，死亡率比全城其余地方还低；接南华克和沃克斯霍尔水的人家，高出好几倍。斯诺的论证是：既然两组在房屋、人口和周围的物质条件上没有任何差别，这样的差距就指向供水。不过，证据中的表九并未限定在混供街道，肯宁顿的数字又不是死亡率，所以这一步仍依赖斯诺“两组没有任何差别”的断言。
paras.en: The author's reading: the two sets of figures point the same way. Kennington's 38 houses against 4 came from the same intermixed streets, though these are only counts of houses with deaths: the evidence does not say how many houses each company supplied there, so they cannot be compared directly as death rates. The table's 315 against 37 covers the houses each company supplied, with the rest of London's 59 falling between them. Houses on Lambeth water died at a lower rate than the rest of the city, houses on Southwark and Vauxhall water at several times it. Snow's argument was that, since there was no difference whatever between the two groups in their houses, the people or their physical surroundings, a gap like this pointed to the water supply. But Table IX in the evidence is not limited to the intermixed streets, and the Kennington figures are not death rates, so that step still rests on Snow's assertion that the two groups did not differ.

heading.en: The parallel run is itself evidence

paras.zh: 一种解释是，这项调查的说服力来自“并行”：两套管道铺在同样的街道上，分组早在两家公司竞争的时候就定下了，没有人为了做实验去改变什么，也就很难说结果是被谁的愿望安排出来的。斯诺本人强调的正是这一点：两组人没有选择，多数也不知情。
paras.en: One reading is that the inquiry draws its force from running in parallel. Two sets of pipes lay along the same streets; the split had been fixed back when the companies were competing, and nobody altered anything to make an experiment, so it is hard to say the result was arranged by anyone's wishes. That is the point Snow himself pressed: the two groups were divided "without their choice" and mostly without their knowledge.

paras.zh: 另一种做法（作者设想的替代方案，不是史实）：只比较各区的平均死亡率，或者拿富区和穷区对比。那样贫富、住房、职业都会混进来，水的作用就分不清了。斯诺实际走的是更费事的路：他亲自查了兰贝斯公司供水所及各区的每一例霍乱死亡，挨家查住址、查水，必要时装瓶回家化验。部分只由南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水的地区（如伯蒙德西等），则由怀廷医生调查疫情头四周；其中部分分区后三周的数字，是按头四周的比例推算的。这样换来了两样东西。一是同一批混供街道里，按供水分开的死亡户数。二是按两家公司全部供水户计算的每万户死亡比较。
paras.en: Another approach, and this is the author's counterfactual rather than history, would have been to compare average death rates by district, or rich districts against poor ones. Wealth, housing and occupation would then have crowded in, and the effect of the water would have been hard to separate out. What Snow actually did was more laborious. He inquired himself into every cholera death in the districts the Lambeth Company supplied: death addresses, house by house, and, where needed, water carried home in phials. Some districts supplied only by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company, such as Bermondsey, were covered for the first four weeks by a medical man, Mr Whiting. In some of those sub-districts the figures for the last three weeks were calculated in the same proportion as in the first four weeks. This yielded two things. One was counts of deaths by water supply for houses in the same intermixed streets. The other was a company-wide comparison per 10,000 houses.

paras.zh: 还有一点容易被忽略（作者的解读）：斯诺没有等调查全部做完才开口。他在肯宁顿查出头一批数字，就交给了法尔；在法尔的建议下，伦敦南部各区的登记员随后被要求为每一例霍乱死亡填报发病房屋的供水。早期的结果先被用来改进收集证据的办法。
paras.en: One more point is easy to miss, and it is the author's reading. Snow did not wait for the inquiry to be finished before speaking. Once he had the first figures from Kennington he passed them to Farr, and at Farr's suggestion registrars in the south districts were asked to return the water supply of the house for every cholera death. The early result went first into improving how the evidence was gathered.

paras.zh: 现代虚构场景一：一家连锁药店的区域主管发现，几家门店的退货投诉似乎集中在同一批货上，手里只有几十条记录。这位主管没有急着宣布结论，而是先把记录交给总部的数据组，请他们在所有门店的退货单上加一栏“批次号”。两周后，答案不再取决于一个人能问到多少家店。
paras.en: Fictional modern scene one. A regional manager at a pharmacy chain notices that returns at a few branches seem to cluster on one batch of stock, with only a few dozen records to go on. Instead of announcing a finding, the manager hands the records to head office's data team and asks for a "batch number" field on every return slip in every branch. Two weeks later, the answer no longer depends on how many shops one person can visit.

paras.zh: 现代虚构场景二：一栋公寓楼里，两家网络公司同时布了线，租客签合同时各选了一家，很多人早忘了自己选的是哪家。半年后楼里有人抱怨视频会议老掉线。物业没有挨户发问卷，而是去查每户墙上的接线盒到底接的是哪家的线，再对照报修记录——同楼、同电梯、同一天的雨，剩下的差别就只有线路。
paras.en: Fictional modern scene two. Two internet providers cabled an apartment block at the same time, and tenants chose one or the other when they signed their leases; many have long forgotten which. Six months on, residents complain that video calls keep dropping. The property manager sends round no questionnaire. Instead, the manager checks which provider's line each flat's wall box is actually connected to, and lays that against the fault reports. Same building, same lifts, same rain — the only difference left is the wire.

paras.zh: 必须说清楚：本篇所有数字与叙述都出自斯诺本人的书和表格。死者住址来自登记总署。8月26日以后，各区登记员应登记总长的要求，填报了霍乱死亡病例发病房屋的供水情况。这些填报并不完整，仍有一批个案的供水没有查明。斯诺写道，这些填报与他对疫情早期的调查结果“完全一致”。这算是来自登记数据的部分印证，不过我们也只是通过斯诺的书才知道这一点。另外，调查并非全部出自斯诺之手：伯蒙德西等一些只由南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水的地区，是由医生约翰·约瑟夫·怀廷（John Joseph Whiting）去调查的。怀廷的调查只覆盖疫情头四周（7月8日至8月5日），查的是死亡发生的房屋接的是公司的水、自家水井还是别的水源；在部分这类分区，后三周的供水是按头四周的比例推算的，并非逐户查得。即便如此，学说、统计的整理以及呈现它们的这本书都出自斯诺；表九的户数基数来自1853年的议会报表，14周统计中两家公司供水户的人口是登记总长的估计数。这不意味着数据有错，但意味着我们读到的是一方的记录。
paras.en: Plainly: every figure and every account in this piece comes from Snow's own book and his own tables. The addresses of the dead came from the General Register Office. After 26 August the district registrars, at the Registrar General's request, returned the water supply of the house of attack in cholera deaths. The returns were incomplete, and the supply "remained unascertained in a number of cases". Even so, Snow says they "agree entirely" with the results of his inquiry into the earlier part of the epidemic. That is partial corroboration from registration data, though it reaches us only through Snow's book. Nor was the whole inquiry Snow's own work. A medical man, John Joseph Whiting, made the inquiries in Bermondsey and certain other districts supplied only by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company. Whiting's part covered only the first four weeks of the epidemic, from 8 July to 5 August, and asked whether each house had the company's water, a pump-well or some other source; in some of these sub-districts the water supply of the last three weeks was calculated in the same proportion as in the first four weeks, not ascertained house by house. Still, the doctrine, the compilation of the statistics and the book that presents them are all Snow's; the house counts behind Table IX come from a return made to Parliament for 1853, and the populations of the houses supplied by the two companies in the 14-week figures were estimated by the Registrar General. That does not make the data wrong, but it does mean we are reading one side's record.

paras.zh: 其次，“两组人没有任何差别”是斯诺的断言，不是随机分组的结果。哪栋房子接哪家水，由当年的房主或住户决定，并非抽签；这种选择会不会和房租、房龄、地段有关，本篇的证据无法回答，这是作者提出的疑问。斯诺自己的调查也显示，按周交租的工人家庭，水费一律由房东或其代理人缴纳，住户对用哪家公司的水一无所知。作者认为，“选择”往往不在喝水的人手里。
paras.en: Second, "no difference whatever" between the groups is Snow's assertion, not the product of random assignment. Which company a house took was decided by the owner or occupier, not drawn by lot; whether that choice tracked rents, the age of the houses or their location is a question the evidence here cannot answer, and it is the author's question. His own inquiry shows that for working families on weekly rents the rates were paid by the landlord or his agent, and the residents did not even know which company supplied them. One reading is that the choice was often not in the hands of the people drinking the water.

paras.zh: 最后，本篇用的是扫描本的OCR文本，书中不少数字在识别时已经错乱，例如兰贝斯迁址的年份被识别成“185S”，化验部分的数值也有乱码。字迹清楚也不等于没有被识别改错：表九“伦敦其余地区”一行的户数与死亡数无法复算出该行的每万户59，本篇只引用其每万户数。因此本篇只用清楚可辨、能够复算的数字，例如表九中两家公司的户数、死亡数和每万户死亡数，以及肯宁顿的分户数字；迁址年份以斯诺脚注中的1852年为准；化验部分只写定性的差别。字迹清楚不等于逐户查得：表九中南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司的死亡数，有一部分是按比例推算的（见上文限定）。
paras.en: Finally, this piece works from OCR text of a scanned copy, and many figures in the book came through garbled: the year of the Lambeth move reads "185S", and the numbers in the chemical test are corrupted too. Legible does not guarantee correctly read: in Table IX the house count and death count for the rest of London cannot be recalculated to give that row's 59 per 10,000 houses, so only the per-10,000 figure is cited for that row. Only figures that are clearly legible and can be checked are used here, such as the two companies' house counts, deaths and deaths per 10,000 houses in Table IX, and the Kennington figures; the year of the move follows Snow's footnote (1852); the chemical test is described only qualitatively. Legible is not the same as ascertained house by house: part of the Southwark and Vauxhall death count in Table IX was calculated in proportion (see the limits above).

scenario.zh: 你负责的流程恰好有两个版本在同一时期并行运行：因为系统迁移的遗留安排，一部分客户走A流程，一部分走B流程，两批人的情况大体相似，但不是随机分配的。现在要定下季度的统一做法，而你手上的数据只跑了几周。
scenario.en: You own a process that happens to be running in two versions at once. Because of legacy arrangements from a system migration, some customers go through version A and some through version B. The two groups broadly resemble each other, but the split was not random. Next quarter you must settle on one standard way of working — and your data is only a few weeks old.

question.zh: 在证据还不完整的时候，你会根据什么改变做法？是等到差异大到无法反驳，还是在差距足够悬殊、且替代解释都能被压住时就行动？你更怕“错在太早”，还是“错在太晚”？
question.en: When the evidence is still incomplete, what would make you change course? Would you wait until the gap is too large to argue away, or act once the difference is stark enough and the rival explanations can be held down? Which mistake frightens you more — being too early, or being too late?

assumptions.zh:
两批客户的情况大体相似，但分组不是随机的，可能存在你没看到的差别（如客户类型、对接人）
只有几周数据，样本不算大，但每一批都完整留痕
换流程本身有成本，不换也有成本
你无法等来完美的实验，只能在现有对照上判断
assumptions.en:
The two customer groups broadly resemble each other, but the split was not random; unseen differences (customer type, account manager) may exist.
Only a few weeks of data; the sample is not large, but both groups left complete records.
Changing the process has a cost; so does not changing it.
No perfect experiment is coming; you can only judge on the comparison in front of you.

steps.zh:
先写清两批人的差别可能来自哪里：除了流程，还有哪些因素能解释结果差异
挑一个最要命的替代解释，找一条能压住它的证据——例如同一类客户里的对比，相当于斯诺在同一批混供街道里所做的比较
只用你确信无误的数据做比较，不引用可疑的细目；把差距换算成直白的说法（比如“前者是后者的几倍”），别急着上复杂模型
给行动设一条线：差距达到多少、替代解释压住到什么程度，就改；达不到就继续观察，但写下复查时间
steps.en:
Write down first where the differences between the two groups could come from: besides the process itself, what else could explain the gap in results?
Pick the most dangerous rival explanation and find one piece of evidence that pins it down — a comparison within the same class of customer, the equivalent of Snow's comparison within the same intermixed streets.
Compare only data you are confident in; skip suspect breakdowns, and turn the gap into plain language (one runs at several times the rate of the other) before reaching for a complicated model.
Set a line for action: how large the gap must be and how well the rival explanations must be pinned down before you switch. Below the line, keep watching — and write down the date to look again.

alternative.zh: 作者提出的另一种做法：暂时两套都留着，把这当成持续进行的对照，等数据再跑一段时间再定。代价是期间有一批客户继续用着较差的流程；好处是避免一次用不完整数据做的全面改动。选哪条，取决于你更在意哪种错。
alternative.en: The author's other option: keep both versions running for now, treat the split as an ongoing comparison, and decide when the data has run longer. The cost is that one group of customers goes on using the weaker process in the meantime; the benefit is avoiding a wholesale change made on incomplete data. Which way you go depends on which error you mind more.

uncertainty_note.zh: 全部数字与叙述出自约翰·斯诺《论霍乱的传播方式》1855年第二版（archive.org 的 OCR 文本）。8月26日以后，各区登记员应登记总长的要求填报了供水情况。这些数据并不完整，斯诺称其与他的结果一致。部分地区的调查由怀廷医生完成；他只调查了疫情头四周，部分分区后三周的供水是按比例推算的。14周的数字把795例供水不明的死亡平均分摊到其他供水来源，两家公司供水户的人口为估计数。这些情况都只能通过斯诺的书得知。“两组没有任何差别”是斯诺本人的断言，分组并非随机。OCR 有错乱，本篇只采用清楚可辨的数字，化验数值未引用。本篇不涉及后世评价与细菌学的后续发展。
uncertainty_note.en: Every figure and account comes from John Snow's On the Mode of Communication of Cholera, 2nd edition (1855), read through archive.org's OCR text. After 26 August, district registrars returned water-supply data at the Registrar General's request. The returns were incomplete, and Snow reports that they matched his results. Part of the inquiry was carried out by a medical man, John Joseph Whiting; he covered only the first four weeks of the epidemic, and in some sub-districts the water supply of the last three weeks was calculated in proportion. The 14-week figures distribute the 795 deaths whose water supply was not ascertained equally over the other sources of supply, and the population of the houses supplied by the two companies is an estimate. All of this is known only through Snow's book. "No difference whatever" between the two groups is Snow's own assertion, and the split was not random. The OCR is garbled in places: only clearly legible figures are used, and the chemical-test values are not cited. Later assessments and the development of bacteriology are not covered.
